hero.title: SQL for Data & Business
hero.subtitle: Learn SQL by writing it. A real query window in every lesson, a retail database to analyse, and labs that run your query and explain what is wrong.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can answer business questions from a database with joins, aggregates, CTEs and window functions, and explain what the numbers mean.

outcomes.title: Query with confidence
outcomes.text: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT and the way NULL really behaves.

outcomes.title: Shape and clean data
outcomes.text: Expressions, CASE, dates, COALESCE and safe division.

outcomes.title: Summarise at scale
outcomes.text: COUNT, SUM, AVG, GROUP BY, HAVING and conditional totals.

outcomes.title: Join without errors
outcomes.text: INNER and LEFT joins, anti-joins and spotting a fan-out before it inflates a total.

outcomes.title: Structure hard questions

outcomes.title: Analyse and explain

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they run your query and explain what is wrong.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Build the channel scorecard, write the memo and pass the final assessment to finish the course.

faq.q: Do I need to install a database?
faq.a: No. The practice window runs a SQL engine in your browser on built-in tables. Your queries never leave your device.

A common core that works in MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and SQLite. The lessons point out where dialects differ, such as date functions. The practice window supports SELECT queries only, so you cannot damage anything.
No. The course starts from what a table is. Comfort with a spreadsheet helps.

Creating or changing tables (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE), indexes and query tuning are mentioned but not practised, because the practice window is read-only. They are the next step after this course.
Finishing every module and the final assessment marks the course complete on your GrowQR profile.

activities.title: Interview the store: customers in Pune
activities.objective: Choose columns, filter rows and sort the result.
activities.scenario: The Pune delivery team wants a list. Show the `name` and `city` of every customer whose city is Pune, sorted by name from A to Z.
steps: Look at the customers table in the panel on the left.
SELECT the two columns FROM customers.
Add WHERE for the city and ORDER BY name.
Run it, then press Check my work.

checks.label: Your query runs without an error
checks.hint: Press Run query and read any message under the editor: it names the problem.
checks.explain: A query that does not run cannot be checked. The message tells you which word or column it could not understand.

checks.label: It uses WHERE to filter the rows
checks.hint: The task needs WHERE to filter the rows. Think about which clause does that job.
checks.explain: WHERE to filter the rows is the clause built for this part of the task.

checks.label: It returns the right rows and columns
checks.hint: Compare the number of rows and columns you get with what the task describes, then check your conditions.
checks.explain: Filter with WHERE city = 'Pune' (text in single quotes), choose the two columns, and sort with ORDER BY name.

spec.solution: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Pune' ORDER BY name

checks.label: The rows are in the order the task asks for
checks.hint: Check the ORDER BY: which column, and ascending or descending?
checks.explain: The task names the sort order; ORDER BY with DESC puts the largest first, and a second column breaks ties.

activities.objective: Handle NULL correctly: a condition on a missing value is neither true nor false.
activities.scenario: The sales team asks for every customer who is **not** in Pune, **including customers whose city was never recorded**. Show only the `name`, sorted by name.

Join the two conditions so that either one is enough.

activities.title: Price list with GST and a band
activities.objective: Calculate new columns and label them with CASE.
activities.scenario: Finance wants a price list. For every product show `name`, `price`, `price_with_gst` (the price plus 18%, rounded to a whole rupee) and `band`: 'premium' for 1000 or more, 'standard' for 300 to 999, otherwise 'budget'. Sort by price, lowest first.
steps: Add the 18% in a calculated column and wrap it in ROUND(..., 0).
Write the band with CASE, highest threshold first.
Name the new columns exactly as the task says, then sort.

checks.label: Your query runs without an error
checks.hint: Press Run query and read any message under the editor: it names the problem.
checks.explain: A query that does not run cannot be checked. The message tells you which word or column it could not understand.

spec.solution: SELECT name, price, ROUND(price * 1.18, 0) AS price_with_gst, CASE WHEN price >= 1000 THEN 'premium' WHEN price >= 300 THEN 'standard' ELSE 'budget' END AS band FROM products ORDER BY price

spec.solution: SELECT name, price, ROUND(price * 1.18, 0) AS price_with_gst, CASE WHEN price >= 1000 THEN 'premium' WHEN price >= 300 THEN 'standard' ELSE 'budget' END AS band FROM products ORDER BY price

activities.scenario: The manager's dashboard needs one row with three numbers from the orders table: `orders` (how many), `completed` (how many have status 'completed') and `customers` (how many different customers placed an order).

activities.title: Share of completed orders by channel
activities.objective: Build a rate with conditional aggregation.
activities.scenario: For each channel show `channel`, `orders` (all orders), and `completed_pct`: the percentage of that channel's orders that are completed, rounded to one decimal place. Sort by channel.
steps: Count the completed rows with SUM(CASE ...).
Divide by COUNT(*) after multiplying by 100.0 so the result is not truncated.
ROUND the percentage to 1 decimal.
